title: Coral and the Salt
premise: Yara Ravensworth, last apprentice of the Saltbound Guild, has spent her life in a valley where magic cannot cross the salt line — until a mute child arrives speaking the Old Tongue, and the valley's protective covenant begins to fail. To save her home, Yara must leave for the first time, journey to the drowned court of the Coral Throne, and discover that her guild once betrayed the realm it swore to protect. As she uncovers her own stolen identity as the covenant's living anchor, she must choose between restoring the old order or forging a new pact that gives power back to those it was taken from. In the end, Yara dissolves the guild's monopoly on magic, seals a renewed covenant sealed by consent rather than blood, and returns home changed — no longer the youngest member of a dying guild, but the first voice of something new.
about_author: Paloma Winterbourne is the pen name of a former tide-pool surveyor who grew up in coastal fishing towns and now writes fantasy from a house perpetually full of sea glass and half-finished maps. Her work explores what justice looks like when the law belongs to the people who broke it first.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She tends the salt line with her dying master, Aldous, chafing at the guild's shrinking purpose and the rule that magic never crosses into the valley. A storm brings a mute child to their door, speaking words that make the salt crystals sing. Emotional beat: restless longing cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Aldous recognizes the child's speech as the Old Tongue of the covenant and panics, burning his records. The child, Tam, draws a drowned city in spilled salt. Yara realizes the guild has been hiding something. Emotional beat: the ground shifting beneath everything she trusted.

chapters.title: What the Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, rendered through his drawings and fragments. He remembers drowning, a throne of coral, hands pulling him from the water. The salt line flickers for the first time in centuries. Emotional beat: fear and grief of a child carrying an adult catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Master's Confession
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. Dying, he admits the guild stole the covenant's anchor generations ago to hoard magic's gatekeeping, and Tam is the realm's plea for repair. He gives Yara a broken key of coral and bone. Emotional beat: shame passed down like an inheritance.

chapters.title: Crossing the Line
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She buries Aldous, takes Tam's hand, and steps over the salt boundary — magic floods her senses painfully. The world beyond is stranger and more alive than any story. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of a first threshold crossed.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the road they meet Brannoc, a disgraced hedge-witch healer who patches Yara's magic-sickness and warns that guild agents hunt them. First act of kindness outside the law. Emotional beat: learning trust can exist without permission.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse of Teeth
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Guild wardens demand passage-tolls paid in memory. Brannoc bargains falsely while Yara and Tam slip through the flooded undercroft. They learn the guild has branded Yara a thief. Emotional beat: the law revealed as a predator's mouth.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They find her ancestral guildhall burned, its archives looted by Warden Corvane, who claims the covenant for himself. Among the ashes, Yara finds a portrait of a woman wearing her own face from two hundred years ago. Emotional beat: identity as a wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Anchor's Name
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. An archive ghost reveals Yara is the original anchor, reborn each generation and bound without consent — the guild's true crime. Tam's arrival woke her early. Emotional beat: rage at discovering your whole self was someone else's instrument.

chapters.title: River of the Unsworn
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They shelter with the Unsworn, outlaws who practice magic freely and justly outside guild law. Their leader, Sefa, offers alliance but wants the coral key as payment. Emotional beat: temptation of trading one cage for another.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He corners Yara, offering legitimacy, restoration of the guild, and safety for Tam if she surrenders the key — he genuinely believes order requires gatekeepers. Emotional beat: seduction of a comfortable injustice.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She refuses; Corvane takes Tam captive and leaves her bleeding. Brannoc saves her life with outlawed craft. Grieving and furious, Yara chooses the Unsworn's path toward the sea. Emotional beat: rock-bottom resolve.

chapters.title: Descent Through Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The company travels sunken roads to the coast, pursued by wardens, losing two of their own. Sefa questions whether Yara will simply become another ruler. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by doubt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a sea cave, the coral key resonates and opens a road beneath the water. Yara walks down alone, breathing salt and light. Emotional beat: awe edged with loneliness — some doors only one person can enter.

chapters.title: Court of the Coral Throne
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the drowned court she faces the Tide Regent, ancient and grieving, who shows her the covenant's original terms: magic shared, not owned. Tam is held here, fading because the court itself is dying. Emotional beat: confronting the scale of the betrayal.

chapters.title: The Price of Repair
chapters.summary: The Tide Regent's POV. The Regent demands the old terms restored — including the anchor's eternal bondage, believing suffering must balance theft. Yara argues for a covenant of consent; the court splits. Emotional beat: justice versus vengeance wearing the same face.

chapters.title: Tam Speaks
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. His voice returns as the court weakens; he testifies that the child sent as a plea chose Yara because she once gave him bread at the valley door — kindness before duty. Emotional beat: the smallest act outweighing centuries of law.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Corvane breaches the drowned court with warden forces, seizing the throne to control the covenant himself. Battle erupts among the coral spires; Sefa's outlaws arrive through the opened gate. Emotional beat: chaos where every faction claims righteousness.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Key
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Realizing the key concentrates power rather than sharing it, Yara shatters it mid-battle, releasing the covenant's magic into all present — wardens included. Corvane, suddenly powerless to command what everyone now holds, collapses. Emotional beat: liberation through destruction of the prize.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Consent
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. With the key destroyed, Yara proposes new terms: no anchor, no gatekeepers, each community swearing its own oath. The Tide Regent, moved by Tam's testimony, consents. The court begins to rise, not drown. Emotional beat: hard-won hope, deliberately imperfect.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She escorts Tam back overland, passing villages already lighting their first lawful-free hearth-fires. Brannoc stays to teach; Sefa rides to spread the terms. Yara dreads and desires returning to the valley that made her. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming anticipated.

chapters.title: Salt and Beginning
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She re-crosses the salt line — which parts willingly now — and founds no guild, but a school, with Tam as its first student in the Old Tongue. Magic hums gently in the valley at last. Final beat: identity chosen, not assigned; justice kept by many hands, not one.
